title: Welcome to the Jungle Broke Even Before It Opened. Then It Earned ₹137 Crore.
excerpt: Director Ahmed Khan revealed the ₹125-crore comedy recouped its entire investment through pre-release deals. With overseas numbers beating OMG 2 and climbing, the Welcome franchise just pulled off Bollywood's most stress-free hit of the year.
body:
Look at the poster for Welcome to the Jungle and try to count the faces. You'll get to twenty before you start losing track. Thirty-four actors share the billing — a number so absurd it loops past criticism and lands somewhere between spectacle and performance art. The film itself has been called overstuffed, chaotic, and review-proof. None of that, it turns out, matters even slightly.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw

Ahmed Khan's comedy has crossed ₹137 crore worldwide in its opening week, with ₹93 crore net from India and ₹26 crore from overseas markets. It is now the 5th highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2026, having overtaken Shahid Kapoor's *O'Romeo* in six days. The next target — *Cocktail 2* at ₹151 crore — is well within striking distance of the second weekend.

But here's the number that actually matters: zero. That's how much Welcome to the Jungle needed to earn at the box office to turn a profit.

The Budget Reveal That Changes Everything

In a conversation with *Zoom*, director Ahmed Khan disclosed that the film's budget never exceeded ₹125 crore — and that the entire investment had already been recouped through digital, satellite, music, and international distribution rights before the first show.

> "I haven't gone beyond ₹115 crore to ₹120 crore, or perhaps ₹125 crore. If you include interest, I haven't surpassed the budget. Now, whatever the film earns is profit. They are fully benefiting from it." — Ahmed Khan

In an industry where a ₹100-crore opening week often isn't enough to save a big-budget film, Welcome to the Jungle was playing with house money from Day 1. Every ticket sold — every rupee of that ₹137 crore worldwide gross — is margin. That's not just a hit. That's a business model.

NRIs Showed Up — and That's the Real Story

For the diaspora, the international numbers tell a quieter but more interesting story. Welcome to the Jungle has earned $774K in North America through six days, with total overseas earnings outpacing OMG 2, Jolly LLB 3, Sky Force, and Bade Miyan Chote Miyan at the same stage. In the post-COVID era, only Housefull 5 and Sooryavanshi tracked better overseas for an Akshay Kumar film at this point.

The Welcome franchise, it turns out, travels. NRI audiences who grew up on the original 2007 film and its 2014 sequel aren't just nostalgic — they're buying tickets. For a comedy that leans heavily on Hindi wordplay, physical gags, and an ensemble cast that includes Suniel Shetty, Arshad Warsi, Raveena Tandon, Paresh Rawal, Johnny Lever, Disha Patani, Jacqueline Fernandez, and Rajpal Yadav, that overseas hold is remarkable. This isn't a *Pathaan*-style spectacle designed for global crossover. It's a very Indian comedy that Indians abroad are choosing to see in theatres anyway — and that tells you something about where the franchise sits in the cultural memory of the diaspora.

The Second Weekend Will Tell the Real Story

The comfortable ride gets a little bumpier starting tomorrow. Alpha, the Alia Bhatt and Sharvari-led YRF spy thriller, opens on July 3 with advance bookings tracking toward a modest ₹7-8 crore opening day. Baby Do Die Do, Huma Qureshi's deaf-mute hitwoman action film, enters the same corridor. Screen allocation will tighten across multiplexes and single screens alike, and Welcome to the Jungle's show count — which held at nearly 10,000 screens on its sixth day — will inevitably shrink.

But the film's real opponent isn't another movie. It's Kesari Chapter 2's lifetime of ₹149.64 crore — the next milestone on Akshay Kumar's worldwide grosser ladder. A strong second weekend gets it there. A decent third week gets it past *Cocktail 2* and into the top 4 Bollywood films of 2026.

For a film that never needed to earn a single rupee at the ticket window to justify its existence, that would be indecent. And entirely on brand for a franchise that has never once apologised for being exactly what it is.
